We work with the notation of the problem. Let

Thus the problem is at least as hard as the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture.

To make the reduction complete, we check that \(\lambda\) is uniformly non-pretentious in the sense of the problem.

For any Dirichlet character \(\chi\), any \(t\in\mathbb R\), and \(N\ge2\),

\[
D(\lambda,\chi n^{it};N)^2
=
\sum_{p\le N}
\frac{1-\operatorname{Re}((-1)\overline{\chi(p)}p^{-it})}{p}

\]

\[
\inf_{|t|\le N} D(\lambda,\chi n^{it};N)\to\infty.
\]

\[
S_N(t)=\sum_{p\le N}\frac{\chi(p)p^{-it}}{p}.

For fixed \(t\), the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions, or equivalently the analytic continuation of \(\log L(s,\chi)\) to the line \(\Re s=1\), gives

\[
S_N(t)=O_\chi(1)

except when \(\chi\) is principal and \(t=0\), in which case

\[
S_N(0)=\sum_{p\le N}\frac{1}{p}=\log\log N+O(1).
\]

Moreover, uniformly for \(|t|\le N\), one has the standard bound

\[
\Re S_N(t)\le \log\log N+O_\chi(1),
\]

with equality only in the pretentious case \(\chi=\chi_0\), \(t=0\). Hence

\[
D(\lambda,\chi n^{it};N)^2
=
\sum_{p\le N}\frac1p+\Re S_N(t)
=
\log\log N+\Re S_N(t).
\]

Therefore, uniformly in \(|t|\le N\),

\[
D(\lambda,\chi n^{it};N)^2
=
\log\log N+O_\chi(1)
\]

when \(\chi=\chi_0\) and \(t=0\), while for all other cases the right-hand side is also \(\log\log N+O_\chi(1)\), and in particular tends to infinity. Thus

\[
\inf_{|t|\le N}D(\lambda,\chi n^{it};N)\to\infty.

So \(\lambda\) is uniformly non-pretentious.

would give

\[
\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N \lambda(n)\lambda(n+1)=o(1).
\]

That is, the conjecture implies the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture for the Liouville function.

Equivalently, any counterexample to the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture would disprove the stated conjecture.

### 2. Notation and the special case

Let

\[
\lambda(n)=(-1)^{\Omega(n)}

\]

**Proof.**  
This is a standard consequence of the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions and the analytic continuation of Dirichlet \(L\)-functions to the line \(\Re s=1\). We give the main line of the argument.

Fix a Dirichlet character \(\chi\pmod q\). Put

\[
S_N(t)=\sum_{p\le N}\frac{\chi(p)p^{-it}}{p}.
\]

Then

\[
\sum_{p\le N}\frac{1+\operatorname{Re}(\chi(p)p^{-it})}{p}
=
\sum_{p\le N}\frac1p+\operatorname{Re}S_N(t).
\]

It is classical that

\[
\sum_{p\le N}\frac1p=\log\log N+O(1).
\]

It therefore suffices to show that

\[
\inf_{|t|\le N}\operatorname{Re}S_N(t)
\ge
-\sum_{p\le N}\frac1p+o(\log\log N)
\]

or, more strongly, that the real part of \(S_N(t)\) is uniformly bounded below by a constant depending only on \(\chi\).

For fixed \(t\), the prime number theorem in arithmetic progressions gives

\[
S_N(t)=O_{\chi}(1)
\]

unless \(\chi\) is principal and \(t=0\), in which case

\[
S_N(0)=\sum_{p\le N}\frac1p=\log\log N+O(1).
\]

The uniformity in \(|t|\le N\) follows from the standard estimate

\[
\left|
\sum_{\substack{p\le N\\p\equiv a\pmod q}}
\frac{p^{-it}}{p}
-\frac1{\varphi(q)}
\sum_{p\le N}\frac{p^{-it}}{p}
\right|
=O_q(1),
\]

valid uniformly for \(|t|\le N\). This is obtained by partial summation from the Siegel–Walfisz theorem. Summing over residue classes \(a\pmod q\) with coefficients \(\chi(a)\), and using

\[
\sum_{a\pmod q}\chi(a)=0
\]

for nonprincipal \(\chi\), we get

\[
S_N(t)=O_{\chi}(1)
\]

uniformly in \(|t|\le N\). Hence

\[
\operatorname{Re}S_N(t)\ge -C_{\chi}
\]

for some constant \(C_{\chi}\). Therefore

\[
\sum_{p\le N}\frac{1+\operatorname{Re}(\chi(p)p^{-it})}{p}
\ge
\log\log N-C_{\chi}
\to\infty.
\]

For principal \(\chi=\chi_0\), the same residue-class argument gives

\[
S_N(t)=\sum_{p\le N}\frac{p^{-it}}{p}+O_q(1).
\]

For \(t=0\),

\[
\operatorname{Re}S_N(0)=\log\log N+O(1).
\]

For \(t\neq0\), the real part of \(\sum_{p\le N}p^{-1-it}\) is uniformly bounded below by a constant. Indeed,

\[
\operatorname{Re}\sum_{p\le N}\frac{1}{p^{1+it}}
=
\sum_{p\le N}\frac{\cos(t\log p)}{p},
\]

and the corresponding integral

\[
\int_2^N \frac{\cos(t\log x)}{x}\,dx
=
\int_{\log 2}^{\log N}\cos(tu)\,du
\]

has a uniform lower bound for \(|t|\le N\). The prime sum differs from the integral by a bounded error. Hence again

\[
\operatorname{Re}S_N(t)\ge -C_{\chi_0}
\]

uniformly, and the desired divergence follows. ∎

**Remark.**  
The lemma is standard. The proof above relies on the Siegel–Walfisz theorem and standard contour integration. We state it as a lemma rather than developing the full analytic machinery here.

### 4. Proof of the reduction theorem

Assuming the lemma, the reduction is immediate.

The conjecture applies to \(f_1=f_2=\lambda\), since \(\lambda\) is uniformly non-pretentious. Taking \(h_1=0\), \(h_2=1\), the conjecture gives

\[
\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N \lambda(n)\lambda(n+1)=o(1).
\]

This is the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture. ∎
